text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It cut from 5.25-5.50% to 4.25-4.50% in three steps: 50 bp in September, then 25 bp each in November and December. The cuts came because inflation had cooled substantially from its 2022 peak and the labor market was softening, so the Fed began easing restrictive policy.

You may be thinking of the zero-rate periods: December 2008 to 2015 (financial crisis) and March 2020 to March 2022 (COVID).
